prompt: In Vertex Cover to Set Cover, graph edges become universe elements and each vertex becomes its incident-edge set. For a star, why does choosing the centre’s set cover the universe?

options.text: The universe consists of the star’s vertices
options.explanation: The universe consists of edges, not vertices.
Its incident-edge set contains every universe element, matching the one-vertex graph cover.

options.text: Every leaf’s set contains every edge
options.explanation: A leaf touches only its own edge.

options.text: Set Cover ignores edges not selected explicitly
options.explanation: Every universe element must be covered, just as every graph edge must be touched.

workedExample: The universe contains edges. The set corresponding to the centre contains every edge of the star; each leaf’s set contains just its own incident edge. Selecting the centre’s set therefore covers the universe and mirrors the one-vertex cover in the original graph.
